evidence.claim: The memory-informed calibration scores this transaction at cms_p=0.02 (cal_p/p_engine=0.0227), far below the real-time risk_score of 0.90 captured on the same transaction.
The $1,000.03 online purchase exceeds this card's prior maximum of $670.04 and prior median of $68.98 as of opening (33 prior transactions, card_seq-1=33), an amount anomaly taken alone.
region_history shows billing region 469.0 is the card's modal/home region with 24 prior purchases across 19 days before opening and hint=home; no roaming or region novelty is present on this alert.

device_history shows prior_n=0 for the flagged device profile on this card as of the flagged timestamp, with device_new_values=['New'] the only value ever seen, consistent with a first-time-device event rather than a fraud signal by itself.

shared_origin_scan shows the flagged device profile is not strong (94 cards in the 30 days before opening, over the 40-card strength ceiling, 208 cards all-time), so despite 11 historical fraud cases on the profile it cannot count as R6 shared-origin evidence.

email_neighbors found 60 cards sharing the recipient domain anonymous.com with this card in the 30 days before opening (e.g. C11923-K2 with 101 txns, C06224-K2 with 93 txns), and shared_origin_scan's domain-level aggregate shows 0 fraud cases for anonymous.com in that same 30-day window, consistent with a high-fanout hub domain rather than a targeted shared-recipient ring.

prior_cases_for_customer shows one closed case on this card, CC-0873, opened 2016-07-21, cleared under a confirmed-travel template with $0 exposure, a weak precedent that a prior risk alert on this card was a false positive.

episode_candidates, card_testing_check and under_threshold_burst confirm the flagged transaction is an isolated singleton (chain n_members=1, no small-authorization run, no bursts), ruling out card_testing and the undocumented under-$500 burst pattern for this alert.

find_similar_cases surfaced 8 closed cases with a same-device overlap (e.g. CC-3954, CC-2720, CC-4362), all confirmed fraud under card_not_present_new_device/card_not_present_fraud, but since this device profile is not strong (94 cards in the 30 days before opening) this reads as base-rate noise from a high-fanout profile rather than distinctive shared-origin evidence.

case.summary: Verdict legitimate at probability 0.05: the $1,000.03 online purchase (txn 3506725) fell in the card's home region, and while the real-time risk_score was 0.90, the memory-calibrated score was 0.02. No episode is scoped (exposure $0.00); the alert could have read as card_not_present_new_device fraud given similar closed cases on the same device profile, but that profile is not strong and a simulated customer_validation reply had the customer confirm the new-device charge. Recommended: CREATE_CASE, ALLOW_TRANSACTION and CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, all auto-route, no approval needed.

initial.reason: 3a: evidence is being requested on this risk-score alert (single-signal, p=0.05) so a case is opened per policy even though the probability sits well below the 0.30 verdict threshold.
R1: single evidence family (risk_score alone, contradicted by cms_p=0.02) and probability 0.05 < 0.70 requires verification with the customer before any further action on this online alert.

final.reason: 3a: a case is opened to record the customer's confirmation of this risk-score alert on transaction 3506725 (exposure $0.00).
R3: the customer confirmed the $1,000.03 purchase, so the transaction is recommended for allow.
R3: customer confirmation plus the low calibrated probability (0.05) across two evidence families (customer, memory) meets the §6 stop rule, so the case is recommended for closing as no fraud.

next_best_actions.what_changed: The assumed customer validation reply (confirm) left the probability at 0.05 and kept the verdict legitimate, adding ALLOW_TRANSACTION, CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, removing VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER. Counterfactual: had the customer denied the purchase, R2 would have applied: BLOCK_CARD (L1) and CREATE_CASE.

stop_reason: Policy §6 test 2 fired: the assumed customer confirmation of the charge settled the question. Independently, probability 0.05 with two evidence families (customer, memory) also meets §6 test 1.
